content.rendered:
The Sea of Galilee at night. A sudden violent storm. Experienced fishermen bailing water in terror. Jesus asleep in the stern. When they woke Him up, He did not pray to the Father about the storm. He spoke directly to it. Three words. The sea obeyed.

The Gospel For Today | Saturday, October 10, 2026 | Teach Me How to Pray, Day 8

Today’s Scripture

“Then He arose and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, ‘Peace, be still!’ And the wind ceased and there was a great calm.”
Mark 4:39 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

The Sea of Galilee lies six hundred and eighty feet below sea level, surrounded by mountains, with a narrow river gorge to the west that funnels cold air down onto the warm surface of the water. The result is a geography famous for sudden, violent, dangerous storms. The disciples, several of whom were professional fishermen on this very body of water, knew the storms better than anyone else in Israel. And on a particular evening recorded in Mark 4, after a long day of teaching from a boat, Jesus said to them, “Let us cross over to the other side.” They set out across the lake with Jesus. He went to the stern, lay down on a cushion, and fell asleep. And then the storm hit. A great windstorm, Mark tells us, with waves beating into the boat so hard the boat was filling with water. The disciples bailed in terror. Then they woke Jesus up with a sentence that gives away the state of their hearts. “Teacher, do You not care that we are perishing?”

Jesus did not pray to the Father about the storm. He did not say, “Father, let this storm pass.” He did not plead for intervention. He stood up, Mark tells us, and spoke directly to the wind and the sea. Three words in Greek. Siōpa, pephimōso. “Peace, be still.” Or more literally, “Be silent, be muzzled.” The verb pephimōso is the perfect passive imperative of the word used for muzzling an animal. Jesus muzzled the storm with a sentence. And the wind, Mark says, ceased. The sea became a great calm. The disciples, who had been afraid of the storm a moment before, were now afraid of Jesus. “Who can this be, that even the wind and the sea obey Him?” They did not yet understand that this is how a Son of God speaks to a circumstance.

The Passion Translation captures the authority of the moment: “Jesus got up and rebuked the storm, ‘Hush! Calm down!’ All at once the wind stopped howling and the water became perfectly calm” (Mark 4:39 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “And He arose and rebuked the wind and said to the sea, Hush now! Be still (muzzled)! And the wind ceased (sank to rest as if exhausted by its beating) and there was [immediately] a great calm (a perfect peacefulness)” (Mark 4:39 AMPC). Muzzled. The language is the language of authority over an animal, not of pleading with a weather system. Jesus spoke to the storm the way a master speaks to a dog.

How Jesus Prayed

The Format. Direct address to the storm. No preamble. No petition to the Father. No lengthy intercession. Three words of command. The format itself teaches the believer that in a crisis, long prayers are not always what is required. Sometimes a short, direct, authoritative command in the name of Jesus is what the moment calls for.

The Essence. The storm was not consulted. The storm was commanded. Jesus related to the storm as something subordinate to His word. The wind had no choice. The sea had no vote. The authority of Christ over natural forces was absolute, and He spoke accordingly.

The Authority. This is one of the clearest demonstrations in the Gospels that the authority Jesus walked in extended to the created order. Wind. Water. Weather. Not just demons and sickness. All creation obeyed His voice. And the same Christ who spoke to the storm then has delegated authority to the believer now. The storms in your life today, whatever form they take, are subordinate to the name of Jesus spoken by a believer who has learned to speak to them, not just about them.

The Assurance. Jesus was asleep in the storm. He had told the disciples before they set out that they were crossing to the other side. The outcome was never in question for Him. When they woke Him in terror, His first words to them were, “Why are you so fearful? How is it that you have no faith?” The assurance of the destination had already been given. The storm was never going to prevent it. The believer who has heard the Father’s word for the day crosses with the same assurance.

The Submission. Jesus spoke to the storm because it was contrary to the Father’s purpose of getting the disciples to the other side. He did not calm every storm He encountered. He calmed this one because it was obstructing the mission. The believer’s authority over storms is always exercised in alignment with the Father’s purposes, not for the believer’s convenience.

The Result. A perfect calm, immediately. The disciples arrived at the other side as Jesus had said they would. For Gospelbuzz readers today, wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, what storm has been beating into your boat this week? Financial. Relational. Emotional. Physical. Learn from Jesus. Do not plead with the Father about it. Speak to it. In the name of Jesus. “Peace. Be still.” The storm has no choice. The authority of the Son is now in you.

Prayer (Pattern After Jesus)

Address (upward). Father, I thank You that You have given me the authority of Christ over the storms of my life. The same Spirit that was in Him when He spoke to the Sea of Galilee is in me now.

Command (outward, to the storm). In the name of Jesus, I speak to the storm of [name the specific storm — the anxiety, the financial crisis, the relational tension, the health scare, the sudden chaos]. Peace. Be still. Be muzzled. You will not sink my boat. The Father has already said I am crossing to the other side.

Faith Declaration. I believe the storm has already obeyed. I am at peace in the boat. I will reach the other side.

In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

The storms in my life are subordinate to the name of Jesus spoken through me. I speak peace to the chaos. I speak stillness to the raging. I will reach the other side the Father has decreed.
